# Browser request ownership: credentials, refresh and caching

[← All question groups](../index.md) · `frontend-http-auth` · **Angular, TypeScript & Frontend Architecture** · Catalog level: senior

<p>Questions come from the preserved source notes. Reframing, assessment intent, senior signals and rubrics are editorial interpretations, not verified model answers or universal interviewer expectations. Follow-ups and the combined production exercise are agent additions. Reading this bank creates no learning record, score, completion or review schedule.</p>

## Start with one representative question

[S06-Q005](#S06-Q005)

<p>How would you coordinate authentication headers and token refresh in an Angular HTTP interceptor when several requests fail authentication together?</p>

## One group objective and observable capabilities

<p>Defend an HTTP-client pipeline that respects credential, retry and response-ownership boundaries.</p>

<ul>
<li>Relate browser credential storage to an explicit threat model.</li>
<li>Trace authentication and overlapping refresh attempts through the interceptor pipeline.</li>
<li>Choose response-cache eligibility, identity and invalidation from the contract.</li>
<li>Define failure tests for sign-out, refresh rejection and stale or misowned data.</li>
</ul>

**Prerequisites**

- [Decide access throughout the token lifecycle](security-token-lifecycle.md)
- [TypeScript guarantees and JavaScript behavior at browser boundaries](frontend-typescript-semantics.md)

<p>Start with who can access credentials and when they leave the browser. That boundary informs how requests acquire authentication and recover from failure. Reusing a response adds another ownership question: data must remain associated with the right identity and freshness contract. These decisions belong to one request flow but require distinct security, retry and cache checks.</p>

### S06-Q009 · Foundation

<p>How do browser storage choices change the risks of keeping authentication information in a web application?</p>

**Source:** [S06-Q009](../../sources/06-frontend-behavioral.md#q009)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S06-Q009](../../sources/06-frontend-behavioral.md#q009)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> How do browser storage choices affect authentication security?

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Compare choices through who can read the credential, when it is sent and how long it remains available. The goal is a threat-based decision, not naming one universally safe storage option.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Relate credential storage to concrete browser threats and authentication boundaries.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Specify browser, authentication architecture, credential type and threat assumptions. Check official browser and identity-provider documentation for relevant storage and cookie behavior.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Separates script access, request transmission and persistence risks in the chosen scenario.</li>
<li>Explains a remaining threat and a test or review that could reveal incorrect credential handling.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Declares a storage mechanism completely secure without stating which threats it addresses.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>What changes if untrusted JavaScript runs in the page?</li>
<li>How would you check whether signing out removes the credential paths your application actually uses?</li>
</ul>

<a id="S06-Q005"></a>

### S06-Q005 · Mechanism

<p>How would you coordinate authentication headers and token refresh in an Angular HTTP interceptor when several requests fail authentication together?</p>

**Source:** [S06-Q005](../../sources/06-frontend-behavioral.md#q005)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S06-Q005](../../sources/06-frontend-behavioral.md#q005)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> How should authentication headers and token refresh interact with HTTP interceptors?

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Explain one request&#x27;s authentication lifecycle and how overlapping requests interact with it. Token refresh means obtaining replacement credentials under the identity provider&#x27;s contract.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Reason about credential handling and concurrent request recovery without an unbounded retry loop.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>State Angular version, token/provider contract, allowed destinations and retryable operations. Consult official framework and provider documentation before relying on specific refresh behavior.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Traces ordinary requests, overlapping refresh attempts and refresh failure.</li>
<li>Identifies credential exposure and replay boundaries with tests that distinguish them.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Retries every authentication failure indefinitely or attaches credentials to every destination.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>What happens to waiting requests when refresh fails?</li>
<li>How would you verify that a retried request cannot duplicate a business operation?</li>
</ul>

</details>

### S06-Q004 · Trade-offs

<p>When is caching an HTTP response inside an Angular interceptor appropriate, and how would you design it for that response contract?</p>

**Source:** [S06-Q004](../../sources/06-frontend-behavioral.md#q004)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S06-Q004](../../sources/06-frontend-behavioral.md#q004)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> How would you implement HTTP caching with an interceptor when caching is actually appropriate?

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>An interceptor can participate in the request and response pipeline. The question asks you to establish when reusing a response is allowed before discussing implementation.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Choose a cache boundary without changing the meaning or ownership of returned data.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Specify Angular version, HTTP cache directives, user or tenant scope, and acceptable freshness. Verify interceptor APIs and HTTP behavior in official documentation.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Justifies eligibility, cache identity and invalidation from the response contract.</li>
<li>Defines tests for stale data, changing identity and repeated requests.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Caches every GET by URL alone, ignoring response ownership and freshness requirements.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>What should happen to cached data after the user signs out?</li>
<li>How would a successful mutation affect the cached response?</li>
</ul>

</details>

## Combined production exercise — agent-added

<p>A SPA displays user-specific orders. Several requests encounter an authentication failure together, while a user signs out and another signs in on the same browser. Design the interceptor flow and decide whether these responses should be cached at all. State the identity-provider contract, permitted request destinations and freshness requirement; propose checks for failed refresh, an overlapping retry and a response arriving after identity changes. Do not assume any provider&#x27;s default behavior.</p>

## Short rubric — use only with an actual attempt

**Basic answer**

<p>Describes adding authentication and handling an ordinary response, with a plausible cache or no-cache choice.</p>

**Senior answer**

<p>Defines credential and response ownership, handles overlap and terminal failure, and justifies retry and cache choices using contracts and discriminating tests.</p>

**Still needs evidence**

<p>Security or cache correctness is asserted without a threat model, identity-transition test, provider contract or response-freshness requirement.</p>
